faq.q: How much of Chilliwack is farmland?
faq.a: The City of Chilliwack states agriculture accounts for 67% of the City's total land base and 29% of its economic activity, and its Official Community Plan carries an Agricultural Area Plan for that land.

Section 6 of Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 sets six agricultural zones: AL (Agricultural Lowland), AU (Agricultural Upland), AS (Agricultural Small Lot), AR (Agricultural Residential), AC (Agricultural Commercial) and AFP (Agricultural Food Processing).

faq.q: How big can a house be on ALR land in Chilliwack?
faq.a: A principal residence built without an ALC application must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction; Chilliwack also applies its Farm Home Plate rules (Development Permit Area 4) to residential building on agricultural land.

faq.q: Can a Chilliwack farm have a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land, one additional residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and City of Chilliwack bylaws must also permit it; the City lists a new house, coach house or suite among the items that may need an ALC application.
